title: Technology in marketing
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T09:32:51Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The closest bank point, E-marketing, covers online channels, targeting and quick measurement, but it does not teach AI, data analytics or the low-cost reach the new point needs, and it is written at NSW Year 12 depth rather than VCE Year 11.

draft.title: Technology in marketing
card: Social media
Platforms where a business posts content and talks with customers. Posts can be low cost and can reach many people.
Email marketing
Sending messages such as offers or news to people who have shared their email address. It is cheap and can be sent to many people at once.
SEO
Search engine optimisation is improving a website so it appears higher in search results. More people then find the business without paid advertising.
AI and data
Artificial intelligence can answer customer questions or suggest products. Data analytics studies customer data, such as past purchases, to learn what customers want.
draft.remember: Marketing technology helps a business reach and learn about customers cheaply.

a.q: Which of these is an example of search engine optimisation?
opts: Improving a website so it ranks higher in search results
Emailing an offer to customers on a mailing list
Posting a video on the business's social media page
Studying past sales to see which products sell best
a.why: SEO means improving a website so it appears higher in search results. Emailing, posting and studying sales data are other tools, not SEO.
a.clue: It is about how high the website appears when people search.

b.q: Tom runs a bakery in Geelong. He studies which items customers bought most over the last six months to decide what to bake. Which tool is he using?
opts: Data analytics
Email marketing
Search engine optimisation
Social media posting
b.why: Tom is studying customer purchase data to learn what customers want, which is data analytics. He is not sending messages, posting content or changing a website.
b.clue: He is looking at past purchase information.

a.best: Improving a website so it ranks higher in search results

problems.detail: The right option is the only one that uses 'search', matching the question's 'search engine optimisation', and it restates the card's definition almost word for word. A student could pick it by matching words without understanding SEO.

check.summary: The facts are accurate and both intended answers are correct. In question a, the right option shares the word 'search' with the question and repeats the card's definition, so students can answer by word-matching.

proposal.title: Technology in marketing
card: Social media
Platforms where a business posts content and talks with customers. Posts can be low cost and can reach many people.
Email marketing
Sending messages such as offers or news to people who have shared their email address. It is cheap and can be sent to many people at once.
SEO

Search engine optimisation is improving a website, such as by using the words people type when they search, so it appears higher in results. More people then find the business without paid advertising.
AI and data
Artificial intelligence can answer customer questions or suggest products. Data analytics studies customer data, such as past purchases, to learn what customers want.
proposal.remember: Marketing technology helps a business reach and learn about customers cheaply.

a.q: Lena rewrites her florist's website so it uses the words people type, such as "flowers Bendigo". What is she most likely trying to do?
opts: Help her site appear near the top when people look online
Collect email addresses so she can send weekly offers
Study past orders to learn which flowers sell best
Gain more followers and comments on her social media
a.why: Using the words customers type helps her website rank higher in results, so more people find her without paid ads. That is SEO. Collecting email addresses is part of email marketing, and changing her website's wording does not send any messages.
a.clue: Think about where those typed words get used by customers.
